title: CRASH-153: hash del key or index decrements nnumofelements after destructor stale count drives uninitialised pointer deref (uninitialised-read)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: our native ASan build of the pinned 5.0.0 tarball (p12, gcc 15.2.0, libasan from gcc 15, 2026-10-27) reports ASAN:SEGV at ext/standard/array.c:1894 in _phpi_pop when trigger.php runs; the corpus records the fix as php-src 86434be9462c, which postdates the release, and names the defect at Zend/zend_hash.c:489-497 (defective ordering: pDestructor at :490, ht->nNumOfElements-- only at :497); faulting consumer ext/standard/array.c:1893-1894
fidelity: the corpus's own trigger script, run through the real interpreter (PHP's cli SAPI, ext/standard only, the port's 145 translation units) rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it. The pristine build crashes on it natively, so a silence on an arm is not a MISSED: the judge reads such a case out of the denominator unless an arm faults at the ASan site.
